notes: The run went fine. Cached data is fast (about 17 GB/s reads and 19 GB/s writes; QueueCache reads cached data about twice as fast). Reading data that is not in the cache yet runs at the bare disk's speed (first read of 1 GiB at 512 MB/s, small random reads at 72 MB/s), because PrimoCache sends several such reads to the disk at once. After a 1 GiB burst the disk caught up in about 7 seconds at about 149 MB/s. With Defer-Write, PrimoCache answers flushes and write-through requests from RAM (a 256 MiB flush returned in 0.17 s, faster than the disk can write) and writes the data to the disk after a delay (10 seconds here). After the simulated power cut the file system was clean and data written earlier had reached the disk, but all 10,000 small files created in the last seconds before the cut were gone.
problems: All 10,000 new small files written in the last seconds before a simulated power cut were lost (the file system stayed clean); flushes are answered from RAM, expected with Defer-Write

Power cuts while part of its held writes were on the disk (churn test): in 1 of 5 checked cuts NTFS needed an offline repair (volume bitmap corruption) and in another NTFS reported a file "corrupted and unreadable"; in the others files written 10-20 s earlier came back with zeros or another file's data, and deleted files came back
